title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. M is a free Z-module of finite type (a lattice Z^n), and (27) is an extension 1 -> M -> G -> H -> 1 with H finite; a crossed-out phrase considered H profinite. So G is a virtually-abelian, crystallographic-type group.

Step 1 (top of page). The finite-index sublattices M_i of M that are stable under H are cofinal among all finite-index sublattices. For each such M_i, G/M_i =: H_i is an extension of H by the finite group M/M_i (eq. 44 on the previous page).

Step 2. Each i gives an exact sequence of group schemes over a base S_0, labelled (45): 1 -> \underline{M}_i -> \mathfrak{G}_i -> H_{S_0} -> 1.
- Here \underline{M}_i is a group scheme attached to the lattice M_i. Plausible readings: the vector group M_i (x) G_a over a Q-base, or the torus M_i (x) G_m; the page does not say.
- \mathfrak{G}_i should be the pushout of the discrete extension G along M_i -> \underline{M}_i, i.e. an algebraic 'hull' of G relative to the lattice M_i.
- As i varies these form a projective system of extensions, i.e. an extension of pro-group-schemes. He regards (\mathfrak{G}_i) as a pro-object in the category of (smooth, etc.) group schemes over S_0.

Step 3. The transition morphisms \mathfrak{G}_j -> \mathfrak{G}_i (for M_j \subset M_i) are affine. The question is local over the base, so it reduces to the homomorphism E(M_i,M_j) -> E(M_i,M_i) = \underline{M}_i.
- E(M_i,M_j) is the extension of the constant finite group (M_i/M_j)_{S_0} by \underline{M}_j, obtained by pushing 0 -> M_j -> M_i -> M_i/M_j -> 0 along M_j -> \underline{M}_j.
- The next page finishes the argument: E(M_i,M_j) is a finite disjoint union of copies of the affine \underline{M}_j, \underline{M}_i is affine, so the map is affine.

Step 4 (next page). Hence the projective limit of the \mathfrak{G}_i is representable by a group scheme, not of finite type. The pro-group depends only on the discrete group G together with the commensurability class of its finite-type abelian subgroups M.

Purpose: in the 'Longue Marche' continuation, this is a way of attaching a pro-algebraic object to a discrete virtually-abelian (and, per the margin 'N-adinisation discrète des groupes résolubles', eventually solvable) group. It is a discrete/algebraic analogue of profinite or N-adic completion, filtered by invariant sublattices.
errors: No mathematical error found. The cofinality claim holds for H finite: intersect the finitely many H-translates of M_i. It also holds for profinite H acting continuously, since the image in GL_n(Z) is then finite.
Gap: the page never states what \underline{M} (the group scheme attached to a lattice) is, nor what S_0 is. The construction is only fully determined in context.
The affineness argument is only sketched: 'the question is local' is asserted. The argument is completed on the next page.

ideas.what: Cofinality of H-stable finite-index sublattices among all finite-index sublattices
ideas.modern_name: standard lemma (normal core of a finite-index subgroup)

ideas.what: Pushing a discrete extension 1->M->G->H->1 along M -> \underline{M} to get group-scheme extensions 1->\underline{M}_i->\mathfrak{G}_i->H_{S_0}->1, assembled into a pro-group scheme indexed by invariant sublattices
ideas.modern_name: algebraic hull / pro-algebraic (Malcev-type) completion of a virtually abelian group; relative completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev; Mostow; Hochschild–Mostow (pro-algebraic hulls); Hain (relative completion)

ideas.what: Affineness of transition maps, so that the projective limit exists as a (non-finite-type) group scheme
ideas.modern_name: existence of limits of affine transition systems (EGA IV §8)

ideas.what: The resulting pro-group depends only on the discrete group G plus a commensurability class of lattice subgroups (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: commensurability invariance of completions / arithmetic-type structure on virtually abelian groups

missed.claim: A sketch of a 'discrete N-adification' of solvable or virtually abelian groups. It produces a pro-group scheme from a discrete group with a commensurability class of lattice subgroups, intended as an algebraic counterpart to the profinite completions used in anabelian geometry. The program for solvable groups indicated in the margin of the previous page is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Pour i variable, elles forment un syst. projectif d'extensions, donc une extension de pro-groupes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is related to relative/pro-algebraic completions of discrete groups (Hain, Pridham) and to profinite rigidity questions for crystallographic groups. It may be a minor precursor, but it is close to known constructions.

deep.surprise_reason: The arguments are routine: core lemma, pushouts, affine transition maps. The idea of a pro-group-scheme completion of a virtually abelian group, depending only on the commensurability class of the lattice, is an interesting unpublished direction in the Longue Marche notes. Close analogues (algebraic hulls, relative completion) exist in the literature, so it would not genuinely surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Equation label is (45), not (41); the previous page already reached (44).
The group symbol is gothic G (\mathfrak{G}_i), matching the next page, not \mathfrak{E}_i.
'(localement ...)' is more likely '(lisses etc ...)', i.e. 'schémas en groupes (lisses etc...) sur S_0'.
The margin probably reads 'prendre des M_i in M !' (or similar).
'sur la base Z' is uncertain; it could be 'sur la base S_0'.
